question: Which of the following Indian Constitutional Amendment Acts is also known as Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**106th Constitutional Amendment Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **106th Constitutional Amendment Bill** is popularly referred to as the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, which translates to "Women Empowerment Act" in English.
 
• It aims to provide **33% reservation for women** in the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People) and the **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• This bill was introduced with the objective of **enhancing the political participation of women** in India, ensuring gender equity in decision-making processes.
 
• The constitutional amendment ensures that the seats reserved for women will rotate periodically among different constituencies, ensuring **fair representation** across all regions.
 
• It highlights India's commitment to achieving **gender equality** as outlined in the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG-5)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The demand for **women’s reservation** in legislative bodies has been a long-standing issue in India, with various political parties and activists advocating for it since the 1990s.
 
• The **84th Amendment Bill** in 1999 and the **Women’s Reservation Bill** introduced in 2008 were earlier attempts that faced hurdles in Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Global Practices:**
 
 
• Countries like **Rwanda**, **Sweden**, and **Norway** have implemented similar measures, with Rwanda having the highest percentage of women in Parliament globally at over **60%**.
 
• India ranks **148th** globally in terms of women’s representation in Parliament, underscoring the need for such reforms.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The **106th Constitutional Amendment** requires the approval of both Houses of Parliament with a two-thirds majority and ratification by at least **50% of state legislatures**.
 
• Once enacted, this reservation will initially apply for a period of **15 years**, after which it may be extended based on necessity.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• This amendment is expected to **bridge the gender gap** in political representation, fostering inclusive governance.
 
• It will provide a platform for women to address issues like **healthcare, education, and gender-based violence** more effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• Article **81** deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha, and this amendment introduces specific provisions for women’s reservation.
 
• Article **170** covers the composition of State Legislative Assemblies, where similar reservations will be applied.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Ensuring the effective implementation of this reservation without political or social resistance may be challenging.
 
• Critics have raised concerns about the potential **tokenism** of women in politics if not accompanied by broader systemic reforms.
 
 
 
• **Way Forward:**
 
 
• Capacity-building programs and leadership training for women are essential to make this reservation impactful.
 
• Efforts to promote gender equality in political parties and grassroots governance structures should complement this amendment.
